mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the cost of capital declines.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 3.5% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points above the prior 3-month average signals a weakening labor market, reducing near-term corporate earnings growth expectations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) below their 6-month moving averages signal a broad-based demand contraction, reducing corporate revenue growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% from 6mo MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% from 6mo MA (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 295), the market anticipates aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations contract under rising discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 295 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions and rising corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations strengthen.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102.0 signals a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain activity, reducing corporate output and earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 102.0 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent weakness in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 below 4-quarter moving average) and declining housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based demand slowdown, reducing corporate revenue growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 < 4q MA and HOUST declines > 0.5% (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During supply shock regimes (INDPRO < 100), reduced industrial output and constrained supply chains increase input costs and inflation expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as equity valuations contract under stagflationary pressures.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 100 (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
